rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guided believers listen, understand, and act on what they know, unlike hypocrites who listen repeatedly without benefit; this contrast also removes the excuse that revelation was obscure.
rows.anchor: فإنه يستمع فيفهم ، ويعمل بما يعلم ، والمنافق يستعيد ، والمهتدي يفسر ويعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided person's understanding and deduction show that the hypocrite's failure comes from blindness of heart, not from any obscurity in the message.
rows.anchor: فإن المهتدي فهم واستنبط لوازمه وتوابعه ، فذلك لعماء القلوب ، لا لخفاء المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible agent of the increase is what they hear from the Prophet, God's words and the Prophet's words, contrasting their understanding with the hypocrites' failure to understand.
rows.anchor: المسموع من النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام من كلام الله وكلام الرسول يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second possibility is that God increases the guided in guidance, just as He seals hypocrites' hearts and increases their blindness.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى زادهم ويدل عليه قوله تعالى : { أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that hypocrites' derision itself increases believers' guidance, since believers find the hypocrites' conduct abhorrent and avoid it.
rows.anchor: الثالث : استهزاء المنافق زاد المهتدي هدى ، ووجهه أنه تعالى لما قال : { واتبعوا أهواءهم }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One transmitted explanation takes the phrase to mean that God gives the guided the reward for their piety.
rows.anchor: قيل فيه إن المراد آتاهم ثواب تقواهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another transmitted explanation takes it to mean that God gives them piety itself, without an implied word, by showing them what piety is.
rows.anchor: وقيل آتاهم نفس تقواهم من غير إضمار ، يعني بين لهم التقوى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third transmitted explanation is that God grants them success in acting on what they have learned.
rows.anchor: وقيل آتاهم توفيق العمل بما علموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī notes that hudā is the verbal noun of هدَى and reads the linked verse as an instruction to follow the guidance by which earlier people were guided.
rows.anchor: والهدى مصدر من هدى ، قال الله تعالى : { فبهداهم اقتده } ( الأنعام : 90 ) أي خذ بما هدوا واهتد كما هدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī proposes that the guided are Quran listeners who understand its meanings and explain them to others, advancing from being guided to guiding others.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد به بيان حال المستمعين للقرآن الفاهمين لمعانيه المفسرين له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the increase moves them from the rank of people guided to the rank of guides, while they avoid speaking about the Quran without proof or interpreting it by personal opinion.
rows.anchor: حتى ارتقوا من درجة المهتدين إلى درجة الهادين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the increase in guidance signals knowledge, while those already guided are careful about matters they do not know, following the best of what they hear and affirming the ambiguous revelation in faith.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الأخذ بالاحتياط فيما لم يعلموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī connects the verse to the preceding rules: faulting or deriding someone for religious difference is permitted, while doing so for other reasons is forbidden under the preceding prohibitions.
rows.anchor: السخرية من الغير والعيب إن كان بسبب التفاوت في الدين والإيمان ، فهو جائز لما بينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apart from faith and disbelief, people share the grounds used for worldly boasting: wealth and lineage can belong to either rich or poor, believer or unbeliever, so these do not establish superiority without piety.
rows.anchor: الناس بعمومهم كفارا كانوا أو مؤمنين يشتركون فيما يفتخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that all people were created from Adam and Eve, so no one should boast over another as all descend from the same two parents.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : من آدم وحواء ثانيهما : كل واحد منكم أيها الموجودون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative is that each person addressed was created from a father and mother, emphasizing that all belong to the same human kind.
rows.anchor: كل واحد منكم أيها الموجودون وقت النداء خلقناه من أب وأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says faith and disbelief produce a profound moral distinction, comparing the unbeliever to livestock or worse and describing the believer as truly human, while all remain one bodily kind.
rows.anchor: لأن الكافر جماد إذ هو كالأنعام ، بل أضل ، والمؤمن إنسان في المعنى الذي ينبغي أن يكون فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An objection says lineage has customary and legal weight, including a restriction on a noblewoman marrying a Nabati.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل هذا مبني على عدم اعتبار النسب ، وليس كذلك فإن للنسب اعتبارا عرفا وشرعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that when religious and divine honor appears, worldly rank by lineage or wealth loses standing, as a great light or sound overwhelms lesser ones.
rows.anchor: إذا جاء الشرف الديني الإلاهي ، لا يبقى الأمر هناك اعتبار ، لا لنسب ولا لنشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious offices such as judgeship and testimony suit any learned, righteous person of high or low status; a profligate is unfit even with Qurashi lineage or great wealth.
rows.anchor: يصلح للمناصب الدينية كالقضاء والشهادة كل شريف ووضيع إذا كان دينا عالما صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If two people share strong religion, lineage can favor one in people's eyes, but not before God, since inherited nobility is not earned through effort.
rows.anchor: إذا اجتمع في اثنين الدين المتين ، وأحدهما نسيب ترجح بالنسب عند الناس لا عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says lineage is singled out among worldly boasts because it is the highest and most stable: wealth can be gained by the poor, and beauty or age do not last.
rows.anchor: النسب أعلاها / لأن المال قد يحصل للفقير فيبطل افتخار المفتخر به ، والحسن والسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation from the same parents and by the same Creator rules out superiority based on origin or maker; only qualities acquired after birth, especially piety and nearness to God, can distinguish people.
rows.anchor: لا ترجيح فيما خلقتم منه لأنكم كلكم من ذكر وأنثى ، ولا بالنظر إلى جاعلين لأنكم كلكم خلقكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading distinguishes dispersed peoples whose common ancestor is unknown, such as non-Arabs, from tribes joined by a known ancestor, such as Arabs and Israelites.
rows.anchor: متفرقة لا يدري من يجمعكم كالعجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading treats the groups as nested ranks: tribes contain peoples, then clans, subdivisions, branches, and relatives.
rows.anchor: فإن القبيلة تحتها الشعوب ، وتحت الشعوب البطون وتحت البطون الأفخاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed purpose of peoplehood and tribes is mutual support rather than boasting.
rows.anchor: أن فائدة ذلك التناصر لا التفاخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī also reads the purpose as mutual recognition rather than estrangement, since mockery, faulting, and backbiting lead to estrangement.
rows.anchor: أن فائدته التعارف لا التناكر ، واللمز والسخرية والغيبة تفضي إلى التناكر لا إلى التعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is the foundation and tribal grouping a later state: people are created for worship and grouped for recognition, so lineage is considered only after worship matters.
rows.anchor: لأن الخلق أصل تفرع عليه الجعل { شعوبا } فإن الأول هو الخلق والإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because neither birth nor tribal assignment comes from people's effort or power, boasting over either is unjustified.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى عدم جواز الافتخاز لأن ذلك ليس لسعيكم ولا قدرة لكم على شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An objection notes that guidance and error are also attributed to God, citing that He guides whom He wills and has shown people the way.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل الهداية والضلال كذلك لقوله تعالى : { إنا هديناه السبيل } ( الإنسان : 3 ) { نهدى به من نشاء } ( الشورى : 52 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī replies that guidance includes human acquisition based on action, as shown by the choice to take a path to one's Lord.
rows.anchor: فنقول أثبت الله لنا فيه كسبا مبنيا على فعل ، كم قال الله تعالى : { فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although human willing remains subject to God's will, lineage itself involves no comparable choice or acquisition.
rows.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله } وأما في النسب فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of knowing one another implies a greater reason to know God: people boast about nearness to a noble ancestor, but God is the noblest being and the worthiest source of honor.
rows.anchor: إنكم جعلتم قبائل لتعارفوا وأنتم إذا كنتم أقرب إلى شريف تفتخرون به فخلقكم لتعرفوا ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride through ancestry either regresses through ancestors or rests on an ancestor's acquired virtue; in the latter case a learned, generous person can surpass the ancestor and has no reason to boast of descent.
rows.anchor: فإن كان بالانتساب لزم الانتهاء ، وإن كان بالاكتساب فالدين الفقيه الكريم المحسن صار مثل من يفتخر به المفتخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī allows that descent from the Prophet is uniquely honorable because no one matches his virtue, then reports the sayings that prophets leave no inheritance while scholars inherit them, interpreting this as acquired rather than genealogical inheritance.
rows.anchor: فقال : ( نحن معاشر الأنبياء لا نورث ) . وقال : ( العلماء ورثة الأنبياء ) أي لا نورث بالانتساب ، وإنما نورث بالاكتساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī recounts hearing of a Khorasani aristocrat descended closely from Ali who was profligate, while a Black freedman advanced through knowledge and good works; the aristocrat insulted him, and the scholar answered that moral conduct made people honor him as the Prophet's heir.
rows.anchor: سمعت أن بعض الشرفاء في بلاد خراسان كان في النسب أقرب الناس إلى علي عليه السلام غير أنه كان فاسقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anecdote's punchline is that the scholar's inner virtue outweighed his black appearance, while people saw the aristocrat's vice rather than his ancestry and treated each by the character he displayed.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الشريف بيضت باطني وسودت باطنك ، فيرى الناس بياض قلبي فوق سواد وجهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī reports two directions of implication: greater piety brings greater honor, or being more honored by God produces greater piety.
rows.anchor: من يكون أتقى يكون عند الله أكرم أي التقوى تفيد الإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative says that whoever is more honored by God is more pious, so divine honor causes piety.
rows.anchor: من يكون أكرم عند الله يكون أتقى أي الإكرام يورث التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading is better known, though Rāzī calls the second more apparent in wording; his example, tastier foods being sweeter, makes honor proportional to piety and establishes piety's priority over other virtues.
rows.anchor: الأول أشهر والثاني أظهر لأن المذكور ثانيا ينبغي أن يكون محمولا على المذكور أولا في الظاهر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that one jurist is harder for Satan to overcome than a thousand worshippers.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لفقيه واحد أشد على الشيطان من ألف عابد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety is the fruit of knowledge, as 35:28 says scholars fear God; a knowledgeable person without piety is a fruitless tree and fuel for Hell, while an ignorant worshipper lacks full God-consciousness.
rows.anchor: نقول التقوى ثمرة العلم قال الله تعالى : { إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address does not imply that unbelievers retain equal honor: all created people initially acknowledged their Lord, but persistence increases their honor and turning away removes its trace.
rows.anchor: نقول ذلك غير لازم مع أنه حاصل بدليل قوله تعالى : { ولقد كرمنا بنىءادم } ( الإسراء : 70 ) لأن كل من خلق فقد اعترف بربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The minimum piety is to fulfill commands and avoid prohibitions without feeling secure or complacent; after a sin one should follow it with good, regret, and repentance rather than rely on time.
rows.anchor: أدنى مراتب التقوى أن يجتنب العبد المناهي ويأتي بالأوامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most pious obeys and abstains while fearing God and attending only to Him; even a moment's turn toward self or child is counted as a fault at this highest rank.
rows.anchor: أما الأتقى فهو الذي يأتي بما أمر به ويترك ما نهى عنه ، وهو مع ذلك خاش ربه لا يشتغل بغير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those at the lower rank are saved, while the highest are brought to the Garden; Rāzī likens the difference to a king's gardener versus a person kept close to the king and granted daily access to estates.
rows.anchor: وللأولين النجاة لقوله تعالى : { ثم ننجى الذين اتقوا } ( مريم : 72 ) وللآخرين السوق إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows outward appearances and lineages as well as inner secrets, so people should make piety their work and increase it as He increases them.
rows.anchor: أي عليم بظواهركم ، يعلم أنسابكم خبير ببواطنكم لا تخفى عليه أسراركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading makes human creation a fresh proof following 50:15, where the earlier creation means the heavens.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون ابتداء استدلال بخلق الإنسان ، وهذا على قولنا { أفعيينا بالخلق الاول } ( ق: 15 ) معناه خلق السماوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading treats the clause as completing the account of human creation, with the earlier creation referring to humanity's first creation.
rows.anchor: وثانيهما : أن يكون تتميم بيان خلق الإنسان ، وعلى هذا قولنا الخلق الأول هو خلق الإنسان أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement may also warn people to turn back from their claims, since God knows every hidden matter and what lies within their breasts.
rows.anchor: تنبيه على أمر يوجب عودهم عن مقالهم ، وبيانه أنه تعالى لما قال : { ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jugular is the vein through which blood runs to every part of the body; although flesh conceals it, nothing conceals anything from God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: والوريد العرق الذي هو مجرى الدم يجري فيه ويصل إلى كل جزء من أجزاء البدن

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison expresses the perfection of God's knowledge: bodily tissue may hide a vein, but nothing can hide from divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: والله أقرب من ذلك بعلمه ، لأن العرق تحجبه أجزاء اللحم ويخفى عنه ، وعلم الله تعالى / لا يحجب عنه شيء

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nearness may refer to God's exclusive power over the person, with His command governing him as blood moves through his veins.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال { ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد } بتفرد قدرتنا فيه يجري فيه أمرنا كما يجري الدم في عروقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī supplies the implied exchange: the condemned blames Satan for making him transgress, and Satan denies it; the next verse's command not to quarrel and parallels in 38:60–64 support this dialogue.
rows.anchor: كأن الكافر حينما يلقى في النار يقول : ربنا أطغاني شيطاني ، فيقول الشيطان : ربنا ما أطغيته

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies the companion with Satan, not the witnessing and recording angel.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : المراد بالقرين في الآية المتقدمة هو الشيطان لا الملك الذي هو شهيد وقعيد

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another commentator identifies the companion as the angel rather than Satan.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره ، المراد الملك لا الشيطان ، وهذا يصلح دليلا لمن قال ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the companion is Satan, the prior declaration that the person is ready for punishment could mean Satan prepared him for Hell through misguidance, apparently conflicting with Satan's denial.
rows.anchor: هذا الشخص عندي عتيد متعد للنار اعتدته بإغوائي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari can reconcile the claims by taking Satan's preparation to mean that he adorned the path, without compelling the person to follow it.
rows.anchor: أن يقول اعتدته بمعنى زينت له الأمر وما ألجأته فيصح القولان من الشيطان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari alternatively places the statements at two moments: Satan first boasts of misguiding humanity, then retracts when he sees their shared punishment and his own penalty.
rows.anchor: وثانيهما : أن تكون الإشارة إلى حالين : ففي الحالة / الأولى إنما فعلت به ذلك إظهارا للانتقام من بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 23 uses a coordinating waw because the soul's arrival with its driver and the witness's speech are conjoined events; verse 27 lacks two such simultaneous meanings, and the preceding fa does not call for a waw here.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن في الأول الإشارة وقعت إلى معنيين مجتمعين ، وأن كل نفس في ذلك الوقت تجيء ومعها سائق ، ويقول الشهيد ذلك القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although one speaker says ربنا, other singular speakers say رب when making personal requests; this scene presents a case with awe rather than asking for an individual favor, so the plural form is apt.
rows.anchor: نقول في جميع تلك المواضع القائل طالب ، ولا يحسن أن يقول الطالب : يا رب عمرني واخصصني وأعطني كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says يوم is most plainly governed by what follows: on the day they are pushed, they are told that this is the fire they denied.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه منصوب بما بعده وهو ما يدل عليه قوله تعالى : { هاذه النار } ( الطور : 14 ) تقديره يوم يدعون يقال لهم هذه النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, يوم can be an appositive for the day in 52:11, the day the deniers are promised and punished.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل غير هذا وهو أن يكون يوم بدلا عن يوم في يومئذ تقريره فويل يومئذ للمكذبين ويوم يوعدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording conveys the terror of Hell: its keepers do not approach it, but shove and cast its inmates in from a distance.
rows.anchor: قوله { يدعون إلى النار } يدل على هول نار جهنم ، لأن خزنتها لا يقربون منها وإنما يدفعون أهلها إليها من بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the verbal noun دعّ presents the shove as a real and undeniable push, like insisting that a trivial blow or weak run does not merit its name.
rows.anchor: الإيذان بأن الدع دع معتبر يقال له دع ولا يقال فيه ليس بدع

rows.speaker: قارئ
rows.claim: On the reading دعاء, the word is an accusative circumstantial expression: they are called to the fire as people summoned to it.
rows.anchor: إلا على قراءة من قرأ { يدعون إلى نار جهنم * دعاء } فإن دعاء حينئذ يكون منصوبا على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of being pushed toward Hell appears to conflict with 54:48, which says they are dragged through the fire.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى : { يوم يسحبون فى النار } ( القمر : 48 ) نقول الجواب عنه من وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reconciliation is that angels drag them through one fire and then, from a distance, cast them into a distinct, hotter Hell; 40:71–72 describes dragging through boiling liquid before kindling in the fire.
rows.anchor: يسحبونهم في النار ثم إذا قربوا من نار مخصوصة هي نار جهنم يقذفونهم فيها من بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reconciliation assigns different stages or tasks to different angels: one pushes them toward the fire and another drags them within it.
rows.anchor: جاز أن يكون في كل زمان يتولى أمرهم ملائكة ، فإلى النار يدفعهم ملك وفي النار يسحبهم آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reconciliation is that chains let them be dragged within the fire while the one pulling them remains outside.
rows.anchor: جاز أن يكون السحب بسلاسل يسحبون في النار والساحب خارج النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth possibility is that angels push them into Hell in humiliation, then enter it themselves and drag them through it.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون الملائكة يدفعون أهل النار إلى النار إهانة واستخفافا بهم ، ثم يدخلون معهم النار ويسحبونهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī supplies an omitted قال: they are told, This is the fire that you used to deny.
rows.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { هاذه النار التى كنتم بها * تكذبون } على تقدير قال
